title: Descent of a bounded principal-open cover
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n,c,d\in\mathbf N$, and $f_i\in R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $R_0\subseteq R$ be a finite type $\mathbf Z$-subring [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and $f_{0,i}\in R_0[x]$ mapping to $f_i$. Write $S_0=R_0[x]/(f_0)$ and $S=R[x]/(f)$. Let $\iota$ be any indexing set and $G_j\in R_0[x]$ for $j\in\iota$. Assume their images avoid every prime of $S$ for at least one $j$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and every nonzero fibre of $R_0\to(S_0)_{\bar G_j}$ has topological Krull dimension at most $d$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then there exist a finite type $\mathbf Z$-subring $R_1\subseteq R$ and equations $f_{1,i}\in R_1[x]$ mapping to $f_i$, such that for each prime $p_1\subset R_1$ whose fibre of $S_1=R_1[x]/(f_1)$ is nonzero, $\iota$ is inhabited and this fibre has dimension at most $d$. In particular, for an empty indexing set $S_1$ is zero. No complete-intersection hypothesis and no lower dimension bound occur in this statement.

proof.text: Apply the proved finite coefficient cover theorem to obtain R₁ containing R₀, finite type over ℤ, on whose polynomial quotient the mapped G_j cover the spectrum. Define f₁,i=map(R₀→R₁)(f₀,i). Composition of coefficient maps and hf₀ show these map back to f_i.

For a prime p₁ of R₁ set p₀=p₁∩R₀. Base change of the naive polynomial-quotient presentation identifies S₁ with R₁ tensor_R₀ S₀, mapping G₁ to 1 tensor G₀. Localization base change and localization of an algebra equivalence identify (S₁)_G₁ with R₁ tensor_R₀ (S₀)_G₀. The residue-field map κ(p₀)→κ(p₁) and two tensor cancellation equivalences identify the p₁-fibre with κ(p₁) tensor_κ(p₀) the p₀-fibre. A nonzero new fibre implies a nonzero old fibre using the ring map from the old fibre into this tensor product. The old fibre is finite type over κ(p₀), by polynomial finite type, quotient finite type, finite type localization away and base-change stability. Transport dimensions along the equivalences and use field-extension dimension invariance, then the given hbound.

Contract any prime of the p₁-fibre to S₁ along tensor includeRight and choose a G_j avoided by this contracted prime. This proves the principal opens of the fibre cover. Since a nonzero fibre has a prime (PrimeSpectrum.nonempty_iff_nontrivial), this also gives an element of ι. Identify each principal open with the spectrum of the localization of the fibre; localization base change identifies its dimension with the corresponding localized p₁-fibre. A zero localization contributes bottom. Every other open has the bound from the previous step. Apply the already proved generic open-cover dimension bound.
